question.problem:
Let $P$, $Q$ and $R$ be three collinear points such that $PQ=7\text{ cm}$ and $QR=13\text{ cm}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. $P$ **cannot** lie between $Q$ and $R$

II. $Q$ **cannot** lie between $P$ and $R$

III. $R$ **cannot** lie between $P$ and $Q$
question.worked_solution:
Let's check each statement.

If $P$ is between $Q$ and $R$, then, by the segments addition postulate, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}QR & =PQ+PR \\ 13 & =7+PR \\ 13-7 & =PR \\ PR & =6\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14182164/assets/d7396a24e0e8884195184a4fca2b4e0fd9cfc2462249c7dc3a0c66901d062c5f.png)

Therefore, $P$ can lie between $Q$ and $R,$ so statement I is false.

If $Q$ is between $P$ and $R$, then again, by the segments addition postulate, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}PR & =PQ+QR \\  & =7+13 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14182164/assets/2dc899f0b5d08bf4a5b5e1833e62e4a3290c8da83dbd376ed51d185c1ed08e94.png)

Therefore, $Q$ can lie between $P$ and $R,$ so statement II is false.

If $R$ is between $P$ and $Q$, then, by the segments addition postulate, we would have:

$$
\begin{aligned}PQ & =PR+QR \\ 7 & =PR+13 \\ PR & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

This can't happen since the length of a segment can't be negative. 

Therefore, $R$ cannot lie between $P$ and $Q,$ so statement III is true.
